problem: The sample-group path rejected four-stage rectangles generated internally by BuildRectListShaders. Its required host FaultBuffer completion was also conservatively classified as an unproved guest memory effect.

implementation.ordinary_pair: Existing SplitDrawShaderRejection remains unchanged and rejects unsafe guest vertex/fragment operations.
implementation.rectangle_provenance: SplitRectListShaderRejection first checks the original guest VS/PS with the ordinary static guard, then regenerates BuildRectListShaders with the actual device target and requires exact intermediate-stage SPIR-V and all current metadata fields.
implementation.intermediate_contract: Exact ordered VS/TCS/TES/PS stages, no missing programs, zero intermediate push-constant offsets, exact 20 DescriptorBinding fields and 19 RecompileResult fields. Arbitrary guest tessellation and mutated diagnostics are rejected.
implementation.target_forwarding: VulkanDevice::Draw materializes and forwards Target only for grouped rectangles. Ordinary rendering incurs no new target construction.
implementation.memory_effects: WritesGuestMemory retains lease, copied-write, guest written range and storage-written checks. Only the already-qualified canonical rectangle path excludes host fault completion from this predicate.
implementation.old_memory_predicate: WritesMemory remains NeedsCompletion OR guest effects. HasCopiedWrites is already part of NeedsCompletion, so adding it to WritesGuestMemory preserves ordinary-path semantics.

source_review.rectangle_geometry: Canonical TCS derives the fourth corner from the real VS three positions, validates finite axis-aligned geometry with equal positive W, and uses fixed tessellation levels of one. TES selects fixed quad vertices. Neither internal stage reads native sample identity.
source_review.repeatable_diagnostic: Canonical TCS claims an independent host FaultBuffer through device-scope CAS, writes uniform InvalidRectangle and zero payload, then publishes Ready with release semantics. Repeated groups do not expose guest writes.
source_review.coverage_limit: This proves no fullscreen coverage. Actual VS output may describe a partial rectangle; viewport/scissor alone do not prove full-surface coverage.
source_review.gpu_limit: Source review supports feasibility; no grouped rectangle GPU pixel-equivalence or game rendering result is asserted.
